item.title: Why the Most Profitable Cartel May Not Last
item.description:
Background

When firms collude to avoid price competition, it seems natural for them to choose the arrangement that produces the largest combined profit. If one firm can produce more cheaply than another, letting it supply the market and share some of the proceeds with its rival would achieve that goal. Yet this paper shows theoretically that a less profitable arrangement can be the only one the firms can sustain.

item.title: How Firms Can Profit by Becoming Less Competitive
item.description:
Background

Firms usually try to become more competitive by expanding capacity, reaching more customers, and lowering costs. When a business closes a plant or leaves a profitable market, we tend to assume that something has gone wrong.

This paper examines theoretically whether deliberately becoming less competitive can encourage industry consolidation through rival mergers and ultimately increase a firm’s own profit.
